note: Byte budgets for the HTML this project ships, closing the bundle half of the performance gap in docs/CONFORMANCE-GAPS.md. Bytes are exact, so these are absolute ceilings with deliberate headroom rather than ratios against a noisy measurement. Raising one is a decision: say why here, in the same commit. Measured by scripts/check_bundle_budget.py, regenerated with its --update flag; tests/test_bundle_budget.py runs the same comparison inside make test and holds the measured block, the rationale figures and the docs/BENCHMARKS.md table to a live measurement, so a stale number here fails rather than sitting quietly under its ceiling.

rationale.playgroundPageBytes: 12 KiB against 11.2 KiB measured. The page is a single self-contained file with no external assets bar the SRI-pinned Pyodide script, and it should stay one screenful of markup plus its boot script. The share-card tags that landed with this commit cost 1.1 KiB: the head carried og:title, og:description and og:url and no image at all, so every share of the playground arrived as grey text. They fit under the existing ceiling, so the ceiling did not move. That leaves 6% headroom rather than the 16% this budget started with, which is the tripwire doing its job: this page is not supposed to grow, and the next addition of this size should be argued for at the time it is needed rather than pre-absorbed by widening the ceiling now. The 1200x630 card itself is a static asset, not markup, and does not enter this figure.
rationale.publishedSiteBytes: 256 KiB against 202 KiB measured. The ceiling was sized when the tree was 110 KiB, so the rule catalog could roughly double before it fired; the per-page meta and canonical tags, and then the share-card tags on all 45 pages, have since taken the tree to 202 KiB, so the remaining headroom is about eleven more rule pages rather than a doubling. The 1200x630 card itself is a static asset, not markup, and does not enter this figure. A build that started emitting something unintended into web/ still fires it.
rationale.publishedPageCount: 60 against 45. One page per rule plus two indexes; 43 rules today. Catches a generator that starts writing pages nobody asked for, which a byte total alone can miss.
rationale.reportBytesAt10kFindings: 3 MiB against 2.24 MiB measured, about 235 bytes per finding. This is the number that can grow silently: a template change adding 80 bytes to a row is invisible on a fixture and adds 800 KB here. FIX-15's contract is that a 10,000-finding report stays usable, and a report that has to be downloaded before it can be read is not.
